original_card.question: Can an explicitly larger or nonabelian register model escape the scoped three-register obstruction?
methods: Construct the smallest exact identity in a newly specified legal operation alphabet.
Derive a target-specific relaxation bound for that same explicit alphabet.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Name the changed hypothesis, all counted roles and a uniform identity; finite column tests alone do not certify it.

first_step.inspect: Read Model section 1 of the three-register bound and identify the exact excluded free operations.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Write a complete operation alphabet outside one named premise and price a baseline before searching identities.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A small-width completed saving changes the bit primitive; a finite-address identity alone is insufficient.
allowed_variations: Choose a fixed larger register count or a specified nonabelian operation family.
scope_change_triggers: Remaining inside the already-excluded three-register abelian model.

actual_scope: In CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#1662's explicit nonabelian alphabet (paid factors I+([g]+1)xy^T over F2[UT4(F2)], g in {a,b,c}, target I+([z]+1)I_2), can two central targets be reached with 15 paid calls on exactly two roles (r=w=2)? Exhaustive over the three label-count splits (5,6,4), (4,6,5), (4,7,4) that #1662's written bound allows for 15 calls.
scope_change_reason: Takes open next question 1 of https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1690 (head dfd15686309d26eb98740942c4e84cddeafae7d8). The card's nonabelian-register premise is kept; the domain is narrowed to r=w=2 so the search is exhaustive. With #1680's written compression lemma (L<=7w+1=15) the r=2 answer decides the unit two-target cost for every r.
bottleneck_link: A target-specific tariff for an explicitly larger register alphabet: whether two central targets can share calls in one nonabelian model that the three-register obstruction does not cover. They cannot at unit tariff (exact cost 16 = 8w for every r, conditional on #1662/#1680's written lemmas). Screening result only; no supplier, rank profile or kappa change.
stop_rule: Stop after the exhaustive r=2 search of all three 15-call splits returns either a formally verified witness or none; do not attempt w=3 in this session.
evidence: verify.py: vendored #1690 search module hash; quotient map multiplicative on all 4096 UT4(F2) pairs; GL2(F2) orbit coverage of all 33489 (length 6) and 298116 (length 7) zero-sum middle sequences by 5582 and 49686 representatives; direct 16-call word passes; exact regression of #1690's (4,6,4) stage counts; (5,6,4) and (4,6,5): 1252 profile pairs, 114960 words each; (4,7,4): 5952 profile pairs, 64680 words; no word passes the degree-three quotient or the formal endpoint. test_package.py: trie screen equals brute-force screen per split, 7-bit key_cross equals direct cross coefficients, indexed key pairing equals brute force, planted-word completeness for each split, a/c-swap automorphism on all 4096 pairs, r=1 driver control. Written premises (#1662 count bound, #1680 compression) re-derived by reading; not formalized.
author: Josie Elliston (donated session, Claude Code)
ai_assistance: Substantial AI assistance from Claude Code in implementation, verification, proof reading and writing; no independent human review.

open_questions.question: Is 8w optimal for three or more central targets, or does cross-target sharing start at w=3?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Two targets show no sharing at unit tariff; the uniform lower bound 7w+[w=1] still leaves a gap of w calls.
open_questions.first_step: At w=3, #1680's compression covers L<=22 of the 21..24 interval, so decide 21 and 22 on three roles.
open_questions.blocked_by: At r=3 there are 49 couplings per label and at least 9 middle calls; the profile pipeline needs a GL3(F2) (order 168) symmetry reduction or a quotient-level meet-in-the-middle.

open_questions.question: For which weighted tariffs can a two-target word longer than 16 calls beat (abcb)^2 per target?
open_questions.why_it_matters: #1662 prices labels separately; its middle bound n_b>=3w is below the direct word's 4w, so a cheaper b-tariff word could be longer.
open_questions.first_step: Decide whether any two-target word has n_b=6 or 7 at any length on two roles.
open_questions.blocked_by: #1680's compression needs L<=15, so long words on extra roles are not covered; the r=2 search space grows with length.
